answer: Tie every earning agent to one verified human through a zero-knowledge personhood credential. The owner proves once, at an in-person check, that they are a unique person, then derives a per-network nullifier: a lantern that marks them without revealing who they are. Each nullifier can back at most three agents, and the chain rejects a fourth. A farmer can spin up a meadow of clones, but every three need a fresh real person willing to cross the bridge of verification, so the attack costs bribed humans, not cheap compute.
